title: Extraction and Safehouse
premise: Isandro Nakamura, a deniable private security contractor, is approached by Mara Voss, a stranger who claims he once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of. The debt she invokes pulls him into a plot to destroy the Kestrel Exchange's Frankfurt data vault during pre-market hours, an attack engineered to read as a catastrophic accident and erase evidence of a decades-old inheritance fraud that stole everything from her family. As Isandro and Mara infiltrate the exchange's security lattice, his own employer turns out to be laundering the fraud's proceeds, forcing him to choose between the contract that defines him and the woman who redefines him. In the end they stop the attack minutes before Frankfurt opens, expose the fraud at terrible cost — Isandro burns his career and identity to do it — and walk away together owing nothing but each other.
about_author: Petra Underhill is a former risk analyst who spent eight years advising financial institutions on physical security before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a farmhouse in the Dolomites, where she is rumored to still consult, anonymously, on cases no one wants attributed.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Wrapping a routine extraction in Marseille, Isandro is cornered by Mara Voss, who thanks him for saving her life in Lisbon three years ago — a city he never worked. She leaves a keycard and a time: 72 hours. Emotional beat: unease; his flawless memory of jobs has a hole in it.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. He verifies the keycard opens a dead drop in Geneva containing surveillance photos of himself he never consented to — and a dossier on the Kestrel Exchange. Someone has been watching him longer than any client. Emotional beat: professional paranoia sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: POV Mara. She explains: her family's fortune was erased by an inheritance fraud buried inside Kestrel's archives, and someone will burn those archives on Thursday morning disguised as an infrastructure accident. She needs him because the Lisbon debt is real — he just doesn't know it yet. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. He refuses; taking sides isn't in his business model. Then his own firm, Halcyon Risk, assigns him to protect Kestrel's executive director — placing him inside the target. Emotional beat: the trap closing with polite corporate language.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Before Dawn
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Arriving in Frankfurt, he maps the exchange's security lattice while shadowing Director Brandt, whose nervousness doesn't match his public calm. He spots a second surveillance team — professionals, not police. Emotional beat: hunter realizing he's also prey.

chapters.title: Lisbon, Reconstructed
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Flashback thread: the real Lisbon incident, where a young contractor pulled her from a staged car crash meant to silence her father. She never learned his name until now. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with guilt over using the debt as leverage.

chapters.title: The Accident Calendar
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Cross-referencing Kestrel maintenance schedules with past 'accidents' at rival institutions, he finds the pattern: every fire was scheduled like a trade. Thursday's window is 07:14, ninety minutes before markets open. Emotional beat: cold clarity — this is a countdown.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Quiet Client
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Digging into Halcyon's books, he finds the firm's anchor client is a trust whose beneficiary structure loops back on itself — the fraud's hiding place. His employer is inside the plot. Emotional beat: betrayal settling in like a diagnosis.

chapters.title: Two Masks at a Gala
chapters.summary: POV alternating. At Kestrel's investor gala, Isandro guards Brandt while Mara works the room as a journalist. They meet publicly for the first time, performing strangers while passing the vault's access rotation under a champagne flute. Emotional beat: intimacy built from deception.

chapters.title: Brandt's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Brandt, drunk and terrified, admits he knows about Thursday and has been paid to be elsewhere. He won't name who pays. Isandro must decide whether protecting his client means protecting the conspiracy. Emotional beat: duty curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: The Second Team
chapters.summary: POV Mara. She identifies the surveillance crew as Vantage Group — the same contractors who staged Lisbon. They've made her. A near-miss escape through the Hauptwache crowds costs her a burner phone and nearly her freedom. Emotional beat: fear she refuses to show him.

chapters.title: What the Debt Was Worth
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Confronting Mara, he demands the truth about Lisbon: she orchestrated their 'chance' meeting; the favor was bait. Fury, then understanding — she had no one else. He stays, not for the debt. Emotional beat: love declared sideways, through choice instead of words.

chapters.title: Vault Nine
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Posing as a compliance auditor, he enters the archive level beneath the trading floor and confirms the fraud documents exist — and that the vault's fire-suppression system has been quietly converted into an accelerant delivery mechanism. Emotional beat: horror at how elegant the murder of truth has been made.

chapters.title: Halcyon Cuts Its Losses
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. His handler orders him to stand down and take leave; his badge dies mid-sentence. Halcyon knows what he found. He goes dark, burning his own operational identity to move freely. Emotional beat: liberation and loss arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: POV Mara. With no firm behind them, they recruit two insiders: a disgruntled vault technician and a BND analyst who owes Isandro from a job in Vienna. Trust is rationed carefully. Emotional beat: fragile fellowship forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Wednesday Night
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Final preparations: the technician will delay the accelerant pump, the analyst will hold a warrant in reserve, Isandro will physically block the ignition sequence, Mara will copy the fraud ledger. Each says goodbye without saying it. Emotional beat: quiet dread and unspoken vows.

POV Isandro. The attack begins early. Vantage's team sweeps the archive level, killing the night supervisor. Isandro reaches Vault Nine's control room seconds behind them, outgunned, improvising. Emotional beat: adrenaline stripped of heroism — pure survival arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Ignition Sequence
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Below, she copies the ledger while alarms cascade; above, Isandro fights the Vantage lead hand-to-hand among the pump manifolds. The technician buys ninety seconds by flooding the wrong sector. Emotional beat: courage as a series of small, terrified decisions.

chapters.title: Accident Denied
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. He kills the ignition at 07:13, one minute before the window, and forces the vault's failsafe open so the BND analyst walks in with lights and cameras — making secrecy impossible. Vantage withdraws into legal fog. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph, already bracing for the price.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Frankfurt opens on schedule; by noon the ledger is with prosecutors and the trust's beneficiaries are named, including Halcyon's founders. Her family's name is restored in a press release she reads standing up, unable to sit. Emotional beat: justice arriving smaller and quieter than imagined.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Halcyon dissolves its leadership; his old handler offers him a clean rebuild with a new name. He declines. Brandt, arrested but alive, asks why Isandro crossed the line. Answer: some contracts you don't sign. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from what survived the fire.

chapters.title: Nothing Owed
chapters.summary: POV both. Weeks later, in Lisbon, they return to the street where it began. Mara formally cancels the debt; Isandro insists on keeping it, reframed — not owed, but chosen daily. They walk toward the river with no client, no cover story, no extraction planned. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved into love as duty, freely kept.
